title: I Can Go Out With My Friends Again (And I'm Not Going Back to Cigarettes)
excerpt: I gave up my social life for almost two years to stay away from smoking triggers. Then I found Piantasia — and got it all back.

children.text: For almost two years, I had a rule: no bars, no nights out, no parties where people smoke.

It sounds extreme. But if you've ever tried to stay off cigarettes, you know exactly what I mean. The moment someone lights up next to you, every bit of resolve you've built over months disappears in about three seconds. One cigarette becomes five. Five becomes a pack. And the next morning you wake up hating yourself, back at square one.
So I made a deal with myself. I chose my lungs over my social life. And for a while, it worked.
But it was lonely.
The Real Cost of Quitting Smoking Nobody Talks About
Everyone celebrates the health wins when you quit — and they're real. But there's a side of quitting that doesn't make it into the motivational posts:
you lose a huge part of your social ritual.
Smoking is woven into how people connect. The cigarette break at a party. Standing outside a bar at midnight talking about everything and nothing. That moment where someone asks
"do you smoke?"
and suddenly you're in a conversation.
When you quit, you don't just lose the cigarette — you lose the social cue that came with it. I didn't know how to stand outside a bar with my hands empty. I felt like a stranger at my own table.
So I stopped going out. It was easier.
How I Found Piantasia

A friend of mine — the same one who later co-founded Piantasia — kept telling me about herbal blends. Tobacco-free, nicotine-free, but actually smokeable. I was skeptical. I'd tried herbal cigarettes before and they tasted like burning grass clippings.

But she showed me what she was working on with Piantasia. Actual thought had gone into it — real herbs, real flavour, real ritual. It wasn't a nicotine replacement. It was a smoking experience without the part that was destroying me.
The first time I tried it I was surprised. It felt
right
. Not like a sad substitute. Like something I could actually enjoy.
The Night I Tested It
There was a birthday party coming up — a close friend, people I genuinely missed. I decided to go, and I brought Piantasia with me.
I won't lie, I was nervous. The first time someone lit a cigarette near me I felt that familiar pull. But I had something in my pocket. I stepped outside, lit a Piantasia, and joined the group.
And that was it. I stood there, talked, laughed, felt part of things again — without the craving spiralling out of control. I smoked one. Then a bit later, another. That was all I needed.
I didn't touch a cigarette that night. Or the next one. Or the one after that.
Why It Works (For Me)
I'm not a doctor and I won't tell you what to do with your body. But here's what I think was happening:
The trigger was never really about nicotine.
It was about the act — the break from the room, the ritual of lighting something, the feeling of belonging to the group outside. Piantasia gave me all of that without the addiction hook.

One or two Piantasia in a social setting is nothing like chain-smoking a packet of cigarettes. The urge that used to feel completely out of control simply... didn't escalate. It had somewhere to go and it stayed there.
I'm Going Out Again
That might sound like a small thing. It isn't.
I went to four events last month. A birthday, a work dinner with drinks after, a Sunday afternoon in a beer garden, a late night with old friends I hadn't seen in years. I was
present
for all of them — not watching the clock waiting to leave, not white-knuckling it in the corner.
Quitting smoking cost me two years of going out. Piantasia gave me back my social life.

If you're in the same position I was — hiding from situations that trigger you, missing people because the risk feels too high — it might be worth trying. Not as a cure, not as a medical solution, just as a ritual that fits where the old one used to be.
You deserve to be in the room.
